tools.name: get_sdn_list_meta
tools.description: Shows which copy of the US Treasury OFAC sanctions list (the SDN list) the checks use: the date Treasury published it, how many entries it holds, when it was copied from Treasury and how many days old that copy is, with a warning if the last daily refresh failed or the copy is more than 14 days old.

tools.name: screen_sdn
tools.description: Checks a name against the latest copy of the US Treasury OFAC sanctions list (the SDN list). Returns match, possible_match, no_match, not_screened or list_behind_schedule, and each listed entry that came close: its name, type, the part that matched, its sanctions programs, and any addresses and ID n

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_sdn_list_meta" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Return the provenance AND the freshness of the loaded OFAC SDN list: source URL, publish date, record count, fetch time, the source + index content hashes, and how many days old the snapshot is against a 14-day staleness threshold (the flag keys on fetch age, not publish age). No input, no PII. Use " → after: "Shows which copy of the US Treasury OFAC sanctions list (the SDN list) the checks use: the date Treasury published it, how many entries it holds, when it was copied from Treasury and how many days old that copy is, with a warning if the last daily refresh failed or the copy is more than 14 days old."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
